questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'The God of Small Things'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The God of Small Things:-**

 
 
• 'The God of Small Things' is a novel set in Kerala, India, and tells the story of fraternal twins Estha and Rahel.
 
• The narrative weaves between their childhood in the late 1960s and their adult lives in the 1990s.
 
• The book explores themes of family, love, caste system, social discrimination, and the tragic consequences of societal norms. 
 
• The story is structured in a non-linear manner, moving back and forth in time, creating a rich tapestry of memories and emotions.​
 
• It delves into the lives of the twins' dysfunctional family, particularly their mother Ammu, their aunt Baby Kochamma, and their half-English cousin Sophie Mol.
 
 
 
• **Arundhati Roy:- **
 
 
• She was born on November 24, 1961, in Shillong, India
 
• She is an Indian author, activist, and public intellectual.
 
• She gained global fame and recognition with her debut novel, 'The God of Small Things,' which won the prestigious Man Booker Prize for Fiction in 1997. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kiran Desai:-**

 
 
• She is an Indian author.
 
• She is the daughter of the famous novelist 'Anita Desai'.
 
• Her novel 'The Inheritance of Loss' won the 'Man Booker Prize' in 2006.
 
• She has also won the 'National Book Critics Circle Fiction Award'.
 
 
 
• **Aravind Adiga:-**
 
 
• Aravind Adiga is an Indian-Australian writer and journalist.
 
• He was born on 23 October 1974.
 
• His debut novel, The White Tiger, won the 2008 Man Booker Prize. 
 
 
 
• ** Khushwant Singh:-**
 
 
• Khushwant Singh is an author, lawyer, diplomat, writer, and politician from India.
 
• He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2007, India's second-highest civilian honour.

questions.question: As of 2022, India is the ________ largest producer of wheat in the world.

__
 
• **Wheat:-**

 
 
• Wheat is a staple crop grown in India.
 
• It is cultivated during the winter months, known as the "Rabi" season.
 
• Major wheat-growing regions include Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Bihar.
 
• **India is the second-largest producer of wheat in the world (as of 2022)**.
 
• Wheat production in India is around 107-110 million metric tons annually.
 
• The government supports wheat cultivation through various schemes and subsidies.
 
• Common wheat varieties grown in India include Sharbati, Sonalika, Durum, Lokwan, and Sharbati, among others.
 
• Irrigation is crucial for wheat cultivation due to the dry winter season.

questions.question: Which is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamet**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Kamet (7,756 metres):

 
 
• ​Kamet, mountain peak of the Himalayas in Uttarakhand state, northern India, 
 
• It is near the border with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
 
• It is part of the Zaskar range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Nanda Devi :

 
 
• It is a part of Himalayan mountain ranges (Garhwal).
 
• This is the highest peak **(7816 metres)** located entirely within India.
 
• The Nanda Devi National Prak, located in vicinity to the peak, consists of the best high altitude flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Nilkantha:-**
 
 
• It is a majestic peak with an elevation of 6,596 meters (21,640 feet) above sea level.
 
• It is a prominent and sacred mountain in the region, and its name is derived from Lord Shiva, who is often referred to as "Nilkantha" (meaning "blue throat") in Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Meru:-**
 
 
• Also known as Meru Peak, is another prominent mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is often confused with Nilkantha due to their similar locations and proximity. Meru Peak is distinct from Nilkantha, and it holds great significance for mountaineers.

questions.question: The British parliament transferred the powers of east India company to the British crown in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The transfer of powers from the East India Company to the British Crown in 1858 was a significant event in British and Indian history.
 
• This event is known as the "Indian Rebellion" or the "Indian Mutiny" of 1857, and it led to the end of the East India Company's rule and the beginning of direct control by the British Crown.
 
• **The events related to this are:**
 
 
• **Indian Rebellion of 1857: **
 
 
• The transfer of powers was a result of the Indian Rebellion that erupted in 1857.
 
• The uprising was a major armed rebellion against the East India Company's rule in India, triggered by various grievances, including the use of cartridges greased with animal fat that offended both Hindu and Muslim soldiers in the British Indian Army.
 
 
 
• **End of East India Company Rule:**
 
 
• Prior to 1858, the East India Company had been governing large parts of India on behalf of the British Crown since the mid-18th century. However, the Indian Rebellion exposed the weaknesses of the Company's rule, leading the British government to take direct control.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1858: **
 
 
• The British Parliament passed the Government of India Act 1858, which is often referred to as the "Act for the Better Government of India."
 
• This act abolished the East India Company's authority and transferred the powers of government to the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **Creation of the Secretary of State for India:**
 
 
• The Government of India Act 1858 established the position of Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British Cabinet and was responsible for overseeing Indian affairs on behalf of the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **India Became a British Colony:**
 
 
• After 1858, India effectively became a British colony, with the British Crown directly controlling its administration and policies.

questions.question: Plants require nutrients for their growth which can be supplied through ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil, water and air.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Plants require nutrients for their growth, which can be supplied through various means:
 
 
• **Soil: The soil contains essential nutrients that plants need, including nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, sulfur, and various micronutrients.**
 
• **Fertilizers:** These are substances added to the soil or applied to plant leaves to provide additional nutrients when the natural soil supply is insufficient. Fertilizers can be organic or inorganic and come in various forms, such as granular, liquid, or slow-release.
 
• **Compost**: Composting organic matter, such as food scraps, yard waste, and manure, produces nutrient-rich compost that can be added to the soil to support plant growth.
 
• **Water: Water serves as a medium for nutrient uptake by the plant roots. Some dissolved nutrients in the soil become available to plants when they are dissolved in water**.
 
• **Hydroponics:** In hydroponic systems, plants grow without soil and receive a carefully balanced nutrient solution directly in water, providing all the essential elements they need for growth.
 
• **Nutrient-rich solutions in labs or controlled environments**: In certain research settings or controlled environments, plants may receive specialized nutrient solutions to study their growth and development under specific conditions.
 
• **Air: It is vital for plants in the process of photosynthesis, as mentioned earlier. During photosynthesis, plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO2) from the air through tiny pores called stomata on their leaves.**

questions.question: Which of the following is 'NOT' an example of communicable diseases?

__
 
• **Communicable diseases:-**

 
 
• A condition brought on by some biological agents or pathogens, such as bacteria, viruses, protozoans, and helminths
 
• Spread between individuals by touch, water, air, food, etc.
 
• Due to their connection to community health, illnesses are a concern for society.
 
 
 
• **Diabetes**:-
 
 
• ​It is a condition that results in high blood sugar levels which is caused by the absence of insufficient production of insulin.
 
• This disease can't be spread from one person to another as it is a non-communicable disease.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is also known as varicella, is a highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus (VZV). 
 
 
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):-**
 
 
• It is a bacterial infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.
 
 
 
• **Common cold:-**
 
 
• It is an acute disease caused by a viral infection that affects the upper respiratory system.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Cell wall is present in animals.
Cell membrane is also called the plasma membrane.
Chromosomes are composed of DNA and Protein.
Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell wall is present in animals. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Cell Wall:-**

 
 
• Cell walls are rigid, protective outer coverings that surround the cells of plants, fungi, algae, and some bacteria.
 
• They provide structural support and protection to these organisms, help maintain cell shape, and prevent the cells from bursting due to osmotic pressure.
 
• **Cell walls are not present in animals.**
 
• In animals, on the other hand, cells are surrounded by a flexible and selectively permeable plasma membrane.
 
• This membrane controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell and serves similar functions to a cell wall, but it is not rigid like a cell wall. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria are often referred to as the "powerhouse of the cell." **

 
 
• This nickname comes from their role in cellular respiration, a process that generates energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
 
• ATP is the primary energy currency that powers various cellular processes within the cell.
 
 
 
• **Chromosomes are composed of a combination of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and proteins. **
 
 
• They are structures within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells that carry genetic information in the form of genes.
 
 
 
• **The cell membrane is also commonly referred to as the plasma membrane. **
 
 
• Both terms are used interchangeably to describe the same structure that surrounds and encloses the contents of a cell.

questions.question: Which among the following is the sole note issuing authority in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI):-**

 
 
• It is the central banking institution of India. It was established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, of 1934.
 
• The RBI is responsible for regulating and controlling the monetary policy of India, **issuing the country's currency (Indian Rupee),** and supervising the banking and financial system to maintain the stability and integrity of the financial sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Industrial Finance Corporation of India:-**

 
 
• It is an Indian government-owned development bank to cater to the long-term finance needs of the industrial sector.
 
• It was the first development finance institution established by the Indian government after independence.
 
• Government established the Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) on 1 July 1948.
 
 
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI):**
 
 
• NPCI operates retail payments and settlement systems,
 
• It is approved by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) To offer improved infrastructure for the entire banking industry to create a robust physical and digital payment and settlement system under the provisions of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
 
• Its main objective is to improve the infrastructure for the entire banking industry to create physical and digital payments.
 
 
 
• 
 
**SBI**:- It is the largest commercial bank in India. It is a public sector bank. Its headquarters is situated in Mumbai, Maharashtra. It is the largest commercial bank in India.

questions.question: With which neighbouring country does India share the Sunderbans forest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sunderbands Forest:-**

 
 
• The name of the Sundarbans forest has been drawn from a mangrove plant known as Sundari (Heritiera Minor). 
 
• This park has been declared as a UNESCO heritage site Because it attracts tourists to this place.
 
• The forest of the Sundarbans is located in the world's largest delta, which is formed by three rivers named the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna.
 
• **India shares the Sunderbans forest with its neighboring country, Bangladesh. **
 
• The Sunderbans Delta is the only mangrove forest in the world inhabited by tigers.
 
• For its preservation, Discovery India and World Wide Fund (WWF) India partnered with the Government of West Bengal and local communities in the Sundarbans in 2019.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: As per census 2011, what is the Total Fertility Rate in India? (provide an approximate range)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.1 - 2.9**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Total Fertility Rate:-**

 
 
• 
 
**It is a demographic indicator that measures the average number of children a woman would have during her reproductive years, usually between the ages of 15 and 49, if she were to experience the age-specific fertility rates observed in a specific population during a specific period.**

 
 
• 
 
TFR is calculated by summing up the age-specific fertility rates (the number of live births to women in specific age groups) and is often expressed as the number of children per woman or per 1,000 women. It is a crucial measure for understanding population dynamics and growth.

 
 
• 
 
A TFR of around 2.1 is considered the "replacement level" fertility rate, meaning that, on average, each woman is having enough children to replace herself and her partner in the population. If the TFR is below 2.1, the population may experience a decline in the long term, while a TFR above 2.1 would result in population growth.

 
 
• 
 
**As per the 2011 census, the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India was approximately 2.1 to 2.9.**

questions.question: ________ are formed when an opaque objects comes in the path of light.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shadows.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shadows:-**

 
 
• These are formed when opaque objects come in the path of light. When light rays hit an opaque object, they are either absorbed or reflected, preventing them from reaching the surface behind the object.
 
• As a result, a shadow is cast on the surface opposite to the light source, creating a darker area.
 
• Shadows provide valuable information about the position, size, and shape of objects, and they play an essential role in various fields such as art, photography, physics, and astronomy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirror reflections:-**

 
 
• It occur when light hits a smooth, reflective surface, such as a mirror, and bounces back in a predictable manner.
 
• The law of reflection governs this phenomenon, stating that the incident angle (the angle between the incoming light ray and the normal, a line perpendicular to the mirror's surface) is equal to the reflected angle (the angle between the outgoing light ray and the normal).
 
 
 
• **Transparent rays:-**
 
 
• It refers to rays of light that pass through a material without being absorbed or scattered significantly.
 
• Transparent materials allow light to pass through them in a straight line, maintaining the direction and intensity of the light rays.
 
• When you look through a transparent material, objects on the other side are clearly visible and not blurred, as the light rays do not get scattered or diffused.

questions.question: Which ministry organised a month-long programme called the 'Kashi Tamil Sangamam' in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Ministry of Education.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Education:-**

 
 
• It is a government department or ministry responsible for overseeing and managing education policies, programs, and systems within a country or jurisdiction.
 
• **Its primary role is to ensure the provision of quality education and promote the development of human capital to meet the needs of the society and economy.**
 
• **Ministry of Education ​organised a month-long programme called the 'Kashi Tamil Sangamam' in 2022.**
 
• The specific responsibilities and functions of a Ministry of Education may vary from country to country, but some common areas they typically address include:
 
 
• **Educational Policies:** Formulating and implementing national or regional educational policies to guide the education system's direction and development.
 
• **Curriculum Development: **Designing and updating the curriculum to meet the educational goals and standards set by the government.
 
• **Teacher Training**: Establishing programs and initiatives to train and develop teachers, ensuring they have the necessary skills and qualifications to deliver quality education.
 
• **School Management: **Overseeing the administration and management of schools, including the allocation of resources and funding.
 
• **Education Quality Assurance: **Monitoring and evaluating the quality of education provided in schools and institutes to maintain high standards.
 
• **Education Funding:** Allocating and managing financial resources for educational institutions and programs.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ministry of External Affairs:-**

 
 
• The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is a government department or ministry responsible for managing a country's external relations and diplomatic affairs with other nations and international organizations.
 
• The primary role of the Ministry of External Affairs is to promote and protect the country's interests and values in the international arena. This ministry plays a crucial role in shaping foreign policy and representing the country's views on global issues.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture **
 
 
• The Ministry of Culture is a government department or ministry responsible for the promotion, preservation, and development of the country's cultural heritage, arts, and traditions.
 
• Its primary role is to nurture and safeguard the nation's cultural identity and diversity while fostering cultural exchanges and creative expressions both within the country and on the international stage.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Tribal Affairs **
 
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is a government department or ministry in certain countries, particularly in India, dedicated to the welfare and development of tribal or indigenous communities.
 
• In India, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs was established to address the specific needs and concerns of the Scheduled Tribes (STs) or Adivasi communities and ensure their overall development and well-being.
